content: Digoxin is often used in combination with other medications to manage atrial fibrillation. It plays a role in controlling the heart rate. Additionally, digoxin may be prescribed for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider. Mechanism of Action: Digoxin works by inhibiting the sodium-potassium ATPase pump in the heart, commonly referred to as the sodium pump. This action increases the force of the heart's contractions while simultaneously lowering the heart rate. Available Forms: Digoxin is available under the brand name Lanoxin and as generic digoxin. It comes in various oral dosage forms, including tablets and a 0.05 mg/mL oral solution. Injectable forms of digoxin are also available. Storage Instructions: Store digoxin at room temperature, between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). It can tolerate short-term exposure to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C), such as during transportation. Always keep it in a cool, dry place. How to Use: Digoxin can be taken as a liquid or tablet that is swallowed, or as a liquid that is injected into a blood vessel or muscle. If prescribed the oral solution, use the provided oral syringe to measure the dose accurately. Consult your pharmacist if you are unsure how to measure your dose. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of digoxin include: Changes in heart rate or rhythm Loss of appetite Nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea Stomach pain or intestinal issues Blurred vision or seeing yellow/green halos Headache Weakness or dizziness Confusion Anxiety, depression, or hallucinations Enlarged breasts in men Skin rash If any of these side effects bother you, inform your healthcare provider. There may be other side effects not listed here. Contact your healthcare provider if you suspect you are experiencing a side effect. Serious Side Effects: While less common, serious side effects of digoxin include: Severe allergic reactions, such as difficulty breathing, wheezing, rapid heartbeat, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, hives, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Changes in heart rate or rhythm, such as bradycardia (slow heart rate), irregular heartbeats, or cardiac arrest. If you experience chest pain, shortness of breath, dizziness, fainting, confusion, or extreme fatigue, contact your healthcare provider immediately. Digoxin Toxicity: Excessive levels of digoxin in the body can lead to toxicity. Symptoms include: Loss of appetite Nausea or vomiting Persistent diarrhea Confusion Weakness Vision changes Abnormal heart rhythms If you suspect digoxin toxicity, stop taking the medication and contact your healthcare provider immediately. Additional medical tests may be required. Precautions: Do not take digoxin if you are allergic to digitalis, digoxin, Lanoxin, or any of the ingredients in the product. Avoid digoxin if you have a specific type of abnormal heart rhythm called ventricular fibrillation. Only take digoxin if it has been prescribed to you by a healthcare provider. Do not share it with others, even if they have the same condition. Keep digoxin out of reach of children. Digoxin may affect your alertness or coordination. Avoid driving or engaging in activities requiring alertness until you know how the medication affects you. Discuss with your healthcare provider how to monitor your blood pressure and heart rate while on digoxin. Before Using Digoxin: Inform your healthcare provider about all your health conditions, including: Wolff-Parkinson-White syndrome Sinus node disease or sick sinus syndrome Atrioventricular (AV) block Kidney problems Myocarditis (inflammation of the heart muscle) Heart failure with preserved left ventricular ejection fraction Thyroid problems Chronic diarrhea Also, disclose any history of electrolyte imbalances, such as low potassium (hypokalemia), low magnesium (hypomagnesemia), low calcium (hypocalcemia), or high calcium (hypercalcemia). Drug Interactions: Digoxin may interact with other medications, including prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, vitamins, minerals, herbal products, and supplements. Inform your healthcare provider about all substances you are taking to avoid potential interactions. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if digoxin can harm an unborn baby. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant. Digoxin passes into breast milk, so discuss with your provider if you are breastfeeding or planning to breastfeed. Food and Alcohol Interactions: The absorption of oral digoxin may be reduced if taken with meals high in bran fiber. It is unclear if alcohol affects digoxin, but drinking alcohol while on digoxin may increase the risk of dizziness, blurred vision, and confusion. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much digoxin, stop using the medication and seek immediate medical attention. Call 911 or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Missed Dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take only the next scheduled dose. Do not take double or extra doses. Uses: Digoxin is primarily used to treat: Heart Failure: It strengthens the heart's contractions and improves blood flow. Chronic Atrial Fibrillation: It helps control the heart rate when the atria and ventricles are not working in sync. Digoxin may also be used for other conditions as determined by your healthcare provider.
